newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila "jeepney" drivers launch protest strikes.
newsitem.headline: Manila "jeepney" drivers launch protest strikes.

text.p: Hundreds of drivers of Manila's popular jeepneys (mini-buses) went on strike on Monday but failed to paralyse transport in the Philippine capital after most drivers refused to join the walkout.

Hardest hit was Makati central business district where up to 80 percent of drivers stayed off the streets, forcing officials to field trucks to ferry hundreds of stranded commuters to work, police sergeant Ronald Ilagan said.
In many other areas, 80 to 90 percent of the colourful jeepneys, Manila's main mode of public transport, were on the road, traffic monitoring officer Cora Manuzon said.
The strikes were spurred by a fuel price increase earlier this month of an average 1.2 U.S. cents per litre.
Several big jeepney organisations refused to join the walkout, saying they were waiting for government action on their petition to raise transport fares.
Jeepneys are World War Two-style jeeps which Filipinos have converted into 16-seat mini-buses.

The price increases were the third since August under an automatic pricing formula based on Singapore posted prices. Diesel oil now costs the equivalent of 29 cents a litre and regular gasoline 36 cents a litre.
The new formula is meant as an interim step towards full deregulation of the Philippine oil industry.
Oil prices in the Philippines were previously strictly controlled by the government.
